h: Dangote cuts petrol price again to ₦1,105 as pump prices fall
p: Major marketers including AA Rano, NIPCO and AP Ardova have reportedly reduced pump prices to between ₦1,350 and ₦1,385 per litre. It follows a ₦51 per litre cut by Dangote Refinery.
body: Motorists are beginning to see some relief at filling stations as major marketers reduce petrol prices following a ₦51 per litre cut by the Dangote Petroleum Refinery.

A market survey on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, reportedly showed that AA Rano, the Nigerian Independent Petroleum Company (NIPCO) and AP Ardova had lowered their petrol prices to between ₦1,350 and ₦1,385 per litre. Several filling stations are said to have cut prices by between ₦20 and ₦60 per litre, with NNPC and other marketers also adjusting their rates.

The reductions come as the cost of importing petrol has dropped, with the landing cost of imported fuel reportedly falling to about ₦1,067 per litre, below Dangote Refinery's own rate. This has put pressure on local prices.
The survey suggested more stations could follow with price cuts in the coming days.

On Thursday, 19 November, Dangote Refinery cut its petrol depot price again, by ₦25 to ₦1,105 per litre, its second reduction in three days. NNPC and other marketers have also been adjusting their prices as competition grows, though final pump prices will depend on supply and transport costs.
more: Dangote's depot price is now ₦1,105 per litre.
It is the second cut in three days.
